lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Discussion or problem seminar: independence stated in conditional terms

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: One approach is shown. There is at least one other that works.

items.prompt: 30 people; 18 do A, 14 do B, 7 do both. Find P(A or B).

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: For each, name a second method before you solve it.

items.prompt: An event has probability 7/8 on a single trial. Two independent trials are run. Find the probability of at least one success, as a fraction in lowest terms.
A survey table records: group X with 13 successes and 47 failures; group Y with 46 successes and 15 failures. Find P(success | group X) as a fraction in lowest terms.
Two events have P(A) = 5/10, P(B) = 9/10, and P(A and B) = 45/100. Are A and B independent?
choices: No; the two events are mutually exclusive.
Yes; P(A and B) equals P(A)·P(B).
No; P(A and B) differs from P(A)·P(B).
Yes; the two events cannot occur together.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: In a group of 59, 29 do activity A, 23 do activity B, and 8 do both. Find P(A or B) as a fraction in lowest terms.
An event has probability 5/11 on a single trial. Two independent trials are run. Find the probability of at least one success, as a fraction in lowest terms.
A survey table records: group X with 30 successes and 34 failures; group Y with 38 successes and 19 failures. Find P(success | group X) as a fraction in lowest terms.

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Argue for one method over another. Say what makes it better, not just that it is.

items.prompt: Two events have P(A) = 9/10, P(B) = 4/10, and P(A and B) = 36/100. Are A and B independent?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: In a group of 34, 14 do activity A, 7 do activity B, and 3 do both. Find P(A or B) as a fraction in lowest terms.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
